'''Grizz Frix''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Homeworld/Legends|from]] [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]] who served as a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. He was raised in a prejudiced society, as Humans on Devaron were in a minority. Since a more tolerant society was impossible under [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] rule, Frix found his escape through piloting. He also read ''[[A Call to Reason]]'' and the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]], and subsequently was inspired to join the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Impressing his recruiter, Frix was assigned to the [[MC80A Home One Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 Star Cruiser]] [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']], and was considered a favorite to join the elite [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] before an accident at [[Gerrard V]] left him psychologically scarred and unfit for active service.

Frix was instead assigned to the [[Support Services/Legends|Alliance Support Services]], escorting refugee [[Starship/Legends|ships]] and fertilizer barges. He learned of the heroic exploits of other pilots through anecdotes and reputation, and his idealistic outlook gave way to that of a hardened cynic. However, with the advent of the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Alliance was in dire need of pilots. Frix was returned to active duty, and he participated in the attack against the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] over [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], piloting a [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]. Frix lost his life during the engagement when he flew too close to the exploding [[ISD-72x deflector shield generator dome|shield generator]] of an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]].

==Biography==
===Joining the Rebellion===
[[File:GrizzFrix-RotJ.png|thumb|right|250px|Grizz Frix joined the Rebel Alliance as a pilot.]]
Grizz Frix was born on mountainous [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]], in the outskirts of a poor town inhabited by both foreigners and [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] natives. Due to the fact that he was an [[Alien/Legends|alien]] amongst the majority of the Devaron populace, he was looked down upon and scorned by fellow citizens. The Devaronians held him in low regard due to his alien nature, and offworlders disliked the fact that he lived amongst what they perceived to be aliens. Frix clamored for a more tolerant and multicultural society, but that was nearly impossible while living under [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] rule. His only escape from the prejudiced environment was the opportunity to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] a dilapidated old [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]], which allowed him to soar high above his home and forget about his worries and his strife.<ref name="db" />

Desperate to break free of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire's]] restrictive hold, Frix was inspired by bootleg copies of former-[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma's]] ''[[A Call to Reason]]'' pamphlet, as well as the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]]. He decided to join the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] as a [[Rebel pilot/Legends|pilot]], and suitably impressed a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] recruiter with his skills. The Sullustan subsequently had him transferred to the [[MC80A Home One Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 Star Cruiser]] [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']]. His enthusiasm and dedication served him well, and he was thought to be a favorite for selection in the elite [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] if his skills improved at a constant rate.<ref name="db" />

Frix's career, however, took a turn for the worse during a training mission on [[Gerrard V]]. His [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]] collided with another [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], requiring him to undertake extensive [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] treatment. He fully healed, but the psychological scars of the ordeal could not be ignored, and although he protested, [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] decided that he was unfit to return to active fighter duty. Instead, he was assigned to [[Support Services/Legends|Alliance Support Services]], escorting refugee supply [[Starship/Legends|ships]] and fertilizer barges to Alliance-controlled [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. He could do nothing but listen to tales told of other pilots, involved in vicious dogfights and epic battles. Soon, Frix shed his idealistic demeanor and became a hardened cynic.<ref name="db" />

===The Battle of Endor===
[[File:GrizzFrixDeath-RotJ.png|thumb|left|220px|The death of Grizz Frix at the Battle of Endor.]]
With the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] massing in the [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]] for their upcoming attack on the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]]<ref name="rotj" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="4ABY" /> High Command decided that they needed every pilot they could get. As a result, Frix was returned to active duty. Despite his cynical new attitude, his enthusiasm for flight that he had experienced on Devaron returned, and he found himself reveling in the opportunity to return to an X-wing cockpit.<ref name="db" /> Frix was partnered with the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-T7]], and he used the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Red Five/Legends|Red Five]]<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Dark Side|pack=(Toys R Us Exclusive) Battle Over Endor (2 of 2)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tvcexbattleoverendor2.asp}}</ref> in [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]], a temporary name for the elite Rogue Squadron.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5 Wedge">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref> He participated in maneuvering exercises shortly before the battle, brushing up on his skills and passing on his knowledge to some of the newer recruits.<ref name="db" />

His nostalgia, however, was short-lived. When the Alliance fleet entered the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], they found that the Death Star II's [[Planetary shield/Legends|shield]] was still active, barring any attack on the superweapon. Even more alarming was the fact that a substantial Imperial [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] was blocking their exit vector, forcing an elongated and bloody [[Battle of Endor/Legends|battle]]. During the chaotic [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfighting]], Frix participated in a daring attack on an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]]. Though the attack resulted in the destruction of one of the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer's]] [[ISD-72x deflector shield generator dome|shield generators]], Frix's X-wing was caught in the ensuing explosion, killing him.<ref name="db" /><ref name="rotj" />

==Personality and traits==
Grizz Frix was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="db" /> with [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]], brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and dark skin<ref name="rotj" /> who stood 1.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall. Due to the fact that he was raised in a prejudiced society, Frix believed from an early age that the Galactic Empire needed to be overthrown. He found solitude in the hours he spent flying his old airspeeder high above the mountains of Devaron. Up there, racial divides were nonexistent, allowing him a brief moment of escape. When he did get the opportunity to fight the Empire, his skills were apparent, and it was only a mishap that prevented him from joining Rogue Squadron, one of the Alliance's most elite corps. The accident on Gerrard V, as well as hearing secondhand tales of heroics, turned Frix into a bitter cynic. Nevertheless, the young idealist he had once been returned, if only briefly, when he was presented with the opportunity to fly in the Battle of Endor,<ref name="db" /> where, as an elite pilot, his defining characteristics were bravery, skill and loyalty. Frix was focused on the goal of victory during the [[Realspace/Legends|space]] battle, and did everything he could to complete his mission, deeply aware he was deciding the future of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Hasbro" />

==Equipment==
Grizz Frix frequently piloted a battered old airspeeder on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. After joining the Rebel Alliance, he was trained in the use of Rebel craft, including the T-65 X-wing starfighter, which he piloted during the Battle of Endor,<ref name="db" /> with the aid of the astromech droid R2-T7.<ref name="Hasbro" /> During his final mission, Frix was equipped with an orange [[Rebel flight suit|flight suit]] and a [[Flight helmet/Legends|flight helmet]] fitted with a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]].<ref name="rotj" /> Frix also carried a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]].<ref name="Hasbro" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I already knew that the character didn't have a happy ending, being killed over Endor, so my strong sense of cynicism (probably a side effect of being British!) wanted to explore a character where he had a wretched life and then had no happy ending&mdash;unlike most of the other characters in Star Wars.|Paul Celer|<ref name="blog1">{{Blog|koruskant|4|A Bitter Pill to Swallow - Behind the scenes of Grizz Frix}}</ref>}}
Grizz Frix was played by [[Ronny Cush]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="jo">{{WebCite|url=http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/entertainment/ronny-cush-_137356|text=Ronny Cush &ndash; A true Jedi|author=Howard Campbell|date=2018-07-01|archivedate=20200130215937}}</ref> wherein the character first appeared as an unnamed pilot who perishes during the Battle of Endor.<ref name="rotj" /> Cush's part was filmed at [[Elstree Studios]],<ref name="tmorotj">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> but much of the recorded footage was not used in the finished film,<ref name="jo" /> and Cush was one of several Rebel pilot actors who were uncredited.<ref name="tmorotj" /> In 2005, [[Paul Celer]], under the pseudonym of "Kast Morben," developed the backstory of the character through the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature "[[What's The Story?]]."<ref name="db" />

[[File:GoldLeaderHelmet-SWC.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Jon Vander's helmet from ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]
Celer, noting how [[George Lucas]] had often given his characters names that gave some indication of their character, such as [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Skywalker]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Solo]], decided to use a play on the word "grizzled," which formed the basis of his character. Celer was interested in the more ordinary people that inhabited the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe, and was inspired by [[Angela Phillips]]'s short story ''[[Slaying Dragons]]'', which was included in the ''[[Tales from the Empire]]'' anthology. Since it was shown in ''Return of the Jedi'' that Frix dies, Celer opted to make his character somewhat of a cynic, with a "wretched life and no happy ending," juxtaposing Frix with the more typical characters that inhabit the original ''Star Wars'' films. Celer also tied the character to two video games, [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] and [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']], through references to Gerrard V and the ''Independence'' respectively. The information about the Sullustan recruiter was added by [[Lucas Online]] in the editing phase&mdash;Celer has suggested that the recruiter might be [[Nien Nunb/Legends|Nien]] or [[Aril Nunb]]. Celer also noted that the character had previously been identified as "Mak Case" in various circles, and he further suggested that this may be an alias for Frix while he was working on the fertilizer barges.<ref name="blog1" />

Rebel flight helmet props created for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] were reused in both [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and ''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="swc">''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref> The helmet worn by Frix in ''Return of the Jedi'' is of the same design as that used by [[Jon Vander/Legends|Jon Vander]] in ''A New Hope'',<ref name="anh">{{Film|IV}}</ref> and [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek Klivian]] in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="esb">{{Film|V}}</ref>
